description: DFHPF3 at app/cbl/COUSR01C.cbl:93-95 moves 'COADM01C' into CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM and performs RETURN-TO-PREV-SCREEN, whose XCTL at :175-178 passes PROGRAM and COMMAREA and no map at all. Four consequences follow and all four are pinned. First, the termination is XCTL and not RETURN_TRANSID: control transfers and does not come back, so the EXEC CICS RETURN at :107-110 is never reached, and the two are not interchangeable. Second, nextMapset and nextMap are absent, because the transfer names no map, whereas every sending path names COUSR01 and COUSR1A. Third, there is no send, so no message reaches a terminal and expectedMessages is empty even though a RECEIVE did happen at :89; POPULATE-HEADER-INFO at :214-233 runs only from inside SEND-USRADD-SCREEN at :184-196, which is why not one header field is pinned here. Fourth, the commarea comes back rewritten in exactly three places by :170-174 - CDEMO-FROM-TRANID 'CU01' at :170, CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM 'COUSR01C' at :171 and CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT zeroed at :174 - while CDEMO-USER-ID and CDEMO-USER-TYPE travel through untouched, because :172-173, which would have set them, are commented out in the source and are not reproduced. The :167 guard IF CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM = LOW-VALUES OR SPACES is evaluated and is false here, because :94 has already stored COADM01C; it is recorded as evaluated rather than as taken. Conversation state travels in the payload and nothing is held on the server, so the sixteen COCOM01Y fields are pinned on both the request and the response, totalling 160 bytes each way. The five typed values are the same ones case01 sends, so the only difference between case01 and this case is the key that was pressed, which is what makes the DFHENTER and DFHPF3 arms of EVALUATE EIBAID at :90-103 separable. PF3 discards them and nothing reaches USRSEC: expectedWrites is empty, and the dataset-level FINAL_STATE expectation pins exactly ten rows of eighty bytes, so a spurious eleventh row is reported as a difference rather than passing in silence, while the ten row-level expectations pin those rows byte for byte. The WRITES channel is deliberately not declared: the recorder reports a dataset on that channel only when a write completed, so a zero-row write expectation here would report a missing dataset instead of the intended statement that nothing was written. Widths are summed mechanically from app/cpy/CSUSR01Y.cpy:17-23 - SEC-USR-ID X(08) at offset 0, SEC-USR-FNAME X(20) at 8, SEC-USR-LNAME X(20) at 28, SEC-USR-PWD X(08) at 48, SEC-USR-TYPE X(01) at 56 and SEC-USR-FILLER X(23) at 57, totalling 80, which app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl:64-73 corroborates with RECORDSIZE(80,80) and KEYS(8,0). The seeds are stated at the 57 characters app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl:35-44 actually carries; the 57-to-80 pad has exactly one owner, the declared USRSEC_FILLER_PAD_57_TO_80 normalisation applied at seed time, and is not pre-applied here. SEC-USR-PWD stays the legacy plaintext X(08) that :157 stores, because hashing it would change behaviour. Preserved rather than improved: :57 COPY DFHATTR is commented out, so no attribute constant is compiled into this program and no attribute expectation appears anywhere in this case, and :172-173 stay silent as described above. This arm never reaches WRITE-USER-SEC-FILE at :238-274, so neither the commented-out DISPLAY of RESP and REAS at :268 nor the 'Unable to Add User...' text of :270-271 is observable here; that EVALUATE WS-RESP-CD WHEN OTHER arm is pinned by case10, which forces the not-found outcome, and by case13, which forces the residual other outcome, while the :251 NORMAL arm is pinned by case01, case11, case12 and case20 and the shared :260-261 DUPKEY and DUPREC arm by case08 and case09. The allocation is stated rather than assumed because this case number is the only coverage of the DFHPF3 arm and of the XCTL-to-COADM01C site. The clock is pinned to 2022-07-19T23:12:34, the instant in the version footer at :298, and is shared by all twenty cases of this folder so nothing depends on wall-clock time; the code page is named explicitly as US-ASCII rather than left to a platform default. expectedReturnCode is 0 because COUSR01C contains no CALL 'CEE3ABD' and never moves to RETURN-CODE, so an online transaction that transfers control still ends at zero. Provenance: every expected value here is statically derived by structured reading of app/cbl/COUSR01C.cbl:78-110, :165-178, :184-196 and :214-233, cross-checked against app/cpy/CSUSR01Y.cpy:17-23's six-field 80-byte layout, app/cpy-bms/COUSR01.CPY:164's ERRMSGO PIC X(78) width, app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD:88-89's FILE(USRSEC) DSNAME binding with ADD(YES) at :93, app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl:35-44 and :64-73, and app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy's title literals. They were not captured from a live COBOL execution: AAP section 0.7.6 proves that impossible in this environment with eight independently verified blockers and records the substitution as risk R-A. No project rules were provided for this repository, so the case is held to the enterprise practices of AAP section 0.10.2 instead.
